_comment: Machine-readable companion to algorithm-presets.md. Consumed by render_assets.py and preflight.sh. The same cipher_suite + ecdh_curves constants appear in the splunk-enterprise-public-exposure-hardening renderer so the two skills agree on the on-the-wire crypto.
_cipher_policy_comment: cipher_policy replaced the former forbidden_cipher_substrings lists. Substring matching could not express these rules: OpenSSL cipher names contain no 'CBC' token (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384 is CBC mode), and SHA-1 suites are spelled '-SHA' not '-SHA1', so both of those entries were permanent no-ops; meanwhile the STIG preset's 'SHA256' entry matched AEAD suites it was never meant to touch. Rules are now expressed against a parsed classification of each suite (skills/shared/lib/cipher_policy.py), and forbidden_tokens compares whole hyphen/underscore-delimited tokens rather than substrings. Enforcement runs at policy load for every preset AND for any operator-supplied --algorithm-policy-file, so a custom cipher list is actually validated rather than merely accepted.

splunk-modern.description: AEAD-only modern cipher set. Derived from Splunk's documented set per https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/install-splunk-enterprise-securely/about-tls-encryption-and-cipher-suites, with the four non-AEAD ECDHE suites removed; see _cbc_removal_note.
splunk-modern._cbc_removal_note: Previously ended with ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA384, ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA256, and ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256. Those four are CBC mode (the names do not say so; openssl ciphers -v reports Enc=AES(n) with no AEAD token) and CBC is listed as deprecated by this repository's own cryptography rules. A preset named 'splunk-modern' offering them contradicted its own name, and because splunk-modern is the default --tls-policy, every operator who did not explicitly choose otherwise got them. Operators with clients that genuinely cannot do AEAD must NOT re-add these here: that silently weakens the default for everyone. Use a separate --algorithm-policy-file carrying a compatibility preset, so the exception is explicit, reviewable, and scoped to the deployment that needs it. See algorithm-presets.md for the concrete procedure.

fips-140-3.description: NIST-approved AEAD only per https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/establish-and-maintain-compliance-with-fips-and-common-criteria-in-splunk-enterprise/secure-splunk-enterprise-with-fips. No CBC, no SHA-1, no anonymous DH, no RSA-1024.

stig.description: DISA STIG-aligned subset of fips-140-3 per splunk-enterprise-public-exposure-hardening/references/disa-stig-cross-reference.md. Refuses RSA-2048 and ECDSA P-256 leaves; requires RSA-3072+ or ECDSA P-384+.
stig._sha256_scope_note: RSA-SHA256 is forbidden as a certificate SIGNATURE algorithm (above), which is the actual STIG requirement. It is deliberately NOT forbidden in cipher_policy. The previous forbidden_cipher_substrings list carried a bare 'SHA256' entry, which conflated two different uses of the same hash name: the signature hash on a certificate, and the PRF/KDF hash of an AEAD cipher suite. As a substring it matched this preset's own ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, so the moment enforcement went live the STIG preset would have rejected its own rendered output. Keeping the two concerns in separate fields is what prevents that recurring.
